stops.note: the formal lament sung over the dead; Eibhlín Dubh Ní Chonaill's Caoineadh Airt Uí Laoghaire (1773), for her murdered husband, is its most famous example
anglicised as 'keen'; paid keening women were a fixture of Irish wakes until the Catholic clergy's disapproval helped the custom fade during the 1800s

current_meaning: a loud wailing lament for the dead
